purpose: Besifloxacin is an antibiotic eye drop used to treat bacterial pink eye, also called bacterial conjunctivitis. It helps clear up the infection in your eye caused by certain bacteria. It is only used in the eyes and is not taken by mouth.
how_it_works: Besifloxacin works by attacking and killing the bacteria that are causing your eye infection. It does this by blocking important processes the bacteria need to survive and multiply. Because it targets the bacteria directly in your eye, it works quickly right where the infection is.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include mild eye irritation, burning, or stinging when you put the drops in. Your eyes may also feel itchy, red, or blurry for a short time after using the drops. These effects are usually mild and go away quickly.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses while you have a bacterial eye infection and while using this medication. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to any antibiotic eye drops or fluoroquinolone medicines. Do not touch the tip of the dropper to your eye or any surface to avoid contaminating the bottle. If your symptoms get worse or do not improve after a few days, contact your doctor.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye three times a day, about 4 to 12 hours apart, for 7 days. Always wash your hands before using the drops. Gently shake the bottle before each use, as the medicine is a suspension.
